questions.question: ________ by the Government of the country makes money acceptable as a medium of exchange.
questions.solution:
• The authorisation is official permission given by a body of power.
 
• For the exchange of goods and services, the seller should receive something of equal value as the good sold.
 
• Money is the entity that is used for this purpose.
 
• While it is the Reserve Bank of India that issues the currency in India, it is done under the authorisation of the Central Government.

questions.question: What is the total strength of (Council of state) Rajya Sabha of India?
questions.solution:
• The Parliament of India is a political body that has the authority to make and amend laws.
 
• It comprises of two houses- Lok Sabha (House of People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• As stated by the Constitution, Rajya Sabha can have a total of 250 members.

questions.question: Who presides over the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Speaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Lok Sabha is the **lower house of the Parliament of India.**
 
• The **Speaker** of the Lok Sabha is the ***person in charge of the Lok Sabha ***and is elected by general elections.
 
• The Speaker serves a term of **five years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Lok Sabha** elects the Speaker** from amongst its members.
 
• The **election date of the Speaker** is determined by the President.
 
• The Speaker** does not vacate** his office when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, and **he/she continues in the position** till the newly elected Lok Sabha meets.
 
• The Speaker is considered as the*** guardian of the powers and privileges of Lok Sabha members.***
 
• The Speaker is responsible for ***maintaining the order and decorum in the House.***

questions.question: Where was the capital of Pallavas?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Pallavas was a dynasty that ruled parts of South India from the 6th to 9th century AD.
 
• The Pallavas made **Kanchipuram (located in Tamil Nadu) **__their capital in the 6th century AD during the reign of Mahendravarman I.

questions.question: Who developed The Ryotwari System?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Ryotwari system was developed by **Thomas Munro**__ and Capt. Alexander Reed in the late 18th century but it was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820 when he became the governor.
 
• The Ryotwari system was a Land Revenue System in British India in which the peasants were given the ownership of the land and the government directly collected taxes from the peasants.
 
• The revenue rate for dry land was 50% and 60% for irrigated land.

questions.question: Maps showing natural features of the Earth are called ________ maps.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A map is a two-dimensional representation of the world which displays the land, water, and other physical features such as roads, rivers, cities, etc.
 
• A relief map is a type of map that displays the 3-D representation of terrain thus showing the mountains and valleys.
 
• These maps are made by contour lines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

**2) Political Maps**

Political maps are designed to show governmental boundaries of countries, states, and counties, the location of major cities, and they often include significant bodies of water. These maps are devoid of topographic features like mountains and valleys but focus on the existence of state and national boundaries and political subdivisions. Political maps are useful for understanding the geopolitical makeup of a region or the world, helping viewers find cities and countries on a map, and identifying administrative boundaries

 

**3. Thematic Maps**

Unlike political maps that focus on geographic boundaries, thematic maps are concentrated on a particular theme or subject matter. This type of map can visualize a wide array of information - such as the spread of a disease, demographic distributions, economic trends, and climate data. Thematic maps can take many forms, including but not limited to, heat maps, choropleth maps, dot distribution maps, and many more. The key characteristic of thematic maps is their ability to communicate specific data sets and variances within them across a defined geography

 

**4. The term "Symbolic" map **isn't a widely recognized category in the traditional classification of maps. Instead, symbolic elements are an integral part of all types of maps. Symbols are used to represent various physical and cultural features. For example, colored lines might represent roads and highways, while different shapes could denote cities, parks, and other landmarks. Symbols are essential for making maps more readable and for compressing complex information into an understandable format. Every map uses symbols to some extent, and these symbols are usually defined in a map's legend or key.

questions.question: Which is the world’s longest river?
questions.solution:

• With a length of about 6,853km, **Nile is the longest river on Earth**__. It flows through northeastern Africa.

questions.question: Oxygenated blood is carried by ___________.
questions.solution:
• The deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle is carried to the lungs by pulmonary artery for oxygenation.
 
• The oxygenated blood from the lungs is then carried by the pulmonary vein to the heart which then pumps this blood to the rest of the body

questions.question: The smallest bone in mammals is ________.

• It is responsible for the mitting the vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear fluid.

questions.question: Cholesterol is related to ________.
questions.solution:
• Organic compounds that do not dissolve in water but are soluble in non-polar solvents like benzene, turpentine, etc. are called lipids.
 
• Fats and cholesterol are related to each other as these are both types of lipids.
 
• They differ in structure and function. While cholesterol is an important constituent of the cellmembrane in animals, fats are macronutrients which are rich in energy.

questions.question: The amount of heat that is produced in a wire when the electric current passes through does not depend on ________.
questions.solution:
• When the electric current passes through a wire, the electrons collide with the surface of the wire which obstructs the movement of the electrons. This is called resistance.
 
• The kinetic energy of the collision gets converted into thermal energy which results in the generation of heat.
 
• According to Joule’s Law of Heating,

H = I²RT

H is the heat generated

 I is the current

R is the resistance of the material

 T is the time of current flow.

Therefore, the heat generated depends on the current, resistance of the material and the time of current flow.

questions.question: Which mirror is used by doctors to examine the eyes, ears, nose, and throat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Concave mirror**.

__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• The mirror which has a spherical reflecting surface is called a spherical mirror.

There are two types of spherical mirror:

Convex mirror:

 
• The spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is away from the center of curvature is called a convex mirror.
 
• It always from a virtual image of any object.

Concave mirror:

 
• The mirror whose reflecting surface is inward is called a concave mirror.
 
• It can form both real as well as a virtual image of any object.

 And for concave mirror image formed when the object is placed at different locations are

if an object is placed beyond the center of curvature then the image will be real, inverted, and diminish

 
• if an object is placed at the center of curvature then the image will be real, inverted and of the same size
 
• if an object is placed at the principal focus image formed in this case will be highly enlarged, real and inverted.
 
• if an object is placed between the principal focus and pole of the mirror then the image will be virtual, erect, and magnified
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0a7b08f7def9b7610813baabc7d001e3e602d85e09c407eaf215cab43a85d09.png] 

Explanation:__

__
 
• When the object is between the center of curvature and focus or between the focus and pole of a concave mirror, the image formed is virtual, erect, and magnified.
 
• Therefore, doctors use concave mirrors__ to examine the eyes, ears, nose, and throat from a close range as the image formed is enlarged and provides a better view to the doctor.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is used as a drying agent?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Calcium chloride**__ is a hygroscopic compound that means it readily attracts and absorbs water molecules from its surroundings.
 
• Calcium chloride binds to the water molecules through crystallisation and is therefore used as a drying agent.
 
• It can also be used to dry solvents like acetone, ethers, esters, etc.

questions.question: An amalgam of metal has which another element?
questions.solution:
• The mixture/alloy of mercury (Hg) with any other metal is called an amalgam.
 
• Tungsten, Platinum, Iron, and Tantalum are exceptions that do not form an amalgam.
 
• Amalgams are extensively used in dentistry, mining, and probes.

questions.question: What is the greenhouse effect?

options.text: Turning of house green because of algae cover
Turning of house green because of the green component of white light
Warming of the Earth because of trapping of radiations by the earth’s atmosphere

questions.solution:
• Greenhouse gases such as methane and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere prevent the rays of the Sun reflected from the Earth’s surface to escape the atmosphere thus trapping the radiations.
 
• The trapped radiations warm the Earth’s atmosphere causing an increase in the global temperature. This is called the greenhouse effect.

questions.question: What is the annual premium (in Rs) of Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)

 
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana is a government scheme launched on 9th May 2015 by PM Narendra Modi in Kolkata.
 
• This is a life insurance scheme that was first introduced by Arun Jaitley, the Finance Minister of India on his 2015 Budget Sheet.
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana is implemented by the Life Insurance Corporation of India.
 
• The basic premium amount for the PMJJBY scheme was INR 330 and reduces thereafter based on the month of your enrollment.
 
• The amount is deducted directly from the associated bank account in an auto-debit manner.
 
• PM Narendra Modi launched three social security schemes the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojna, the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, and the Atal Pension Yojana.
 
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana was launched by the Central Government of India that provides life coverage to the poor and low-income section of society.
 
• The scheme offers a maximum assured amount of Rs. 2 lakhs.
 
• The premium rate of PMJJBY has been revised in 2022 upward to Rs 1.25 per day, translating into an increase from Rs 330 to Rs 436 annually.
 
• Apart from this, **the annual premium for PMSBY has been increased from Rs 12 to Rs 20.**
 
• **These new premium rates were effective from June 1, 2022.**

questions.question: Who invented the first ever safety elevator?
questions.solution:
__
 
• A safety elevator was a modification of primitive elevators which prevented the platform from falling in case the cable broke.
 
• It was invented by **Elisha Otis**__ in 1852.
 
• On 23rd March 1857, the first passenger safety elevator was installed at 488 Broadway in New York.

questions.question: Bombayala Devi is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
• A member of the national recurve team, Bombayala Devi Laishram is an archer who represents India in archery at international level.
 
• She won a silver medal at the World Archery Championship, 2011.
 
• She was awarded the Arjuna Award in 2012.

questions.question: Boat races of Kerala are special feature of which festival?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Boat races of Kerala are a special feature of **Onam__.**
 
• __**Onam**__ is the harvest festival of Kerala which is celebrated to welcome King Mahabali.
 
• Depending on the Malayalam Calendar, the festival falls in the month of August or September and lasts for 4-10 days.
 
• Celebrations involve songs, dance, games, and feasts.
 
• The **Snake Boat Race** called **Vallamkali** is carried out on the Pampa river with hundreds of people racing and chanting folk songs.

questions.question: Who has won the Madhav Rao Scindia Award for most runs in Ranji Trophy for the year 2015 – 16?
questions.solution:
• Madhavrao Scindia Award is a part of the BCCI Awards which are annual awards given to cricketers for their achievements in that year.
 
• In 2015-16, Shreyas Santosh Iyer was awarded the Madhavrao Scindia Award for the most runs in the Ranji Trophy. He scored a total of 1321 runs.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book named 'Born Again on the Mountain’?
questions.solution:
• Arunima Sinha was a National Volley Ball player who lost her leg after she was pushed out of a moving train by thieves.
 
• Born Again on the Mountain is the autobiography of Arunima Sinha that details her struggle post accident and her subsequent achievement in mountaineering.
 
• It was published in 2014.

questions.question: 'India-Africa Forum Summit’ is an official platform for the African-Indian relations which is held every _____ years.
questions.solution:
• The India-Africa Forum Summit was first carried out in New Delhi from 4th April 2008 to 8th April 2008 and has since been held every 3 years.
 
• This summit aims at strengthening the relations between the two countries by providing a platform for discussion on trade, security, technology, agriculture and peace.

questions.question: The Madhesi tribe is related to India and its neighbouring country _____.
questions.solution:
• Madhesi is a group of Nepalese people who live in the Terairegion of Nepal but are Indian in origin.
 
• These people migrated to Terai in the late 18th century due to the availability of agricultural land and subsidies offered to new settlers.
